.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 212 PM EDT Tuesday...

No significant changes have been made to the forecast.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 233 PM EDT Tuesday...

1. A weak cold front will bring some shower chances to the 
region tomorrow, with seasonable and mostly dry conditions 
prevailing through the remainder of the week.

2. Showery and cooler conditions with beneficial rain are on 
track for late this weekend into early next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 212 PM EDT Tuesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Mostly dry and seasonable conditions are 
expected to continue across the region through the remainder of 
the week, with a few chances for showers possible. High 
temperatures will generally be in the 70s to low 80s the next 
several days. Another round of patchy fog will be possible 
tonight into tomorrow morning with high pressure overhead, but 
moisture will be limited which will influence how much fog 
develops overnight. A decaying cold front will move through the 
region tomorrow, bringing chances for scattered showers and 
possible embedded thunderstorms, particularly across northern 
New York. Showers and any thunderstorms that do develop look to 
be rather unimpactful, with limited dynamics and instability to 
promote any stronger thunderstorms. Shower chances may linger 
into the evening, especially across the higher terrain before 
drier conditions return to the region. Some showers cannot be 
entirely ruled out on Thursday as a weak area of low pressure 
moving across southern New England, but chances are fairly low 
and dry conditions are expected to prevail across most of the 
area, with dry and seasonable conditions continuing into Friday.

KEY MESSAGE 2: A deep 500 millibar trough is expected to dig 
into the Great Lakes region Saturday night, leading to 
widespread showers overspreading our area into Sunday. Expect 
showers will tend to be orographically enhanced with this setup,
but thankfully there are are no signals for noteworthy moisture
or heat to advect northward, which limits potential for 
impactful/hazardous weather. As such, the latest 48 hour 
rainfall probabilities of exceeding 1.00" of rain are only in 
the 15 - 40% range with 2.00" probabilities below 10%. Greatest 
chances of the higher rainfall amounts appear primarily in the 
western foothills of the Adirondacks and westward into the St. 
Lawrence Valley. Given the aforementioned meridional winds and 
likely deep upper level low, would expect a fairly long duration
event with at least periods of showers. Generally this system 
should bring plenty of cloud cover and cool air from the 
northwest by Monday, such that daytime temperatures will trend 
temporarily below normal before recovering towards midweek 
following the departure of the trough.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
Through 00Z Thursday...The return of radiation fog is possible 
tonight around 06Z-14Z Wednesday, most likely IFR level for a 
couple hours at the typical sites SLK and MPV. Due to drier air 
mixing down this afternoon as compared to yesterday's increased 
moisture following the rain, the anticipated fog coverage and 
longevity tonight is much less than last night. There may also 
be more southwesterly winds just aloft during the prime fog 
hours tonight from return flow, and clouds are likely to be on 
the increase, especially across northern New York. Overall, we 
continue to see mixed signals on when and for how long fog is 
going to develop in the valleys, but expect it will be more 
isolated and shorter duration than last night. On Wednesday, 
winds will increase out of the south-southwest, resulting in 
channeled gusts at MSS 15-20 knots by the afternoon hours. We 
also expect showers to arrive from west to east across northern 
New York Wednesday morning, arriving at MSS by 11Z-19Z.
